name: Pale Purple-Drab
lede: Pale Purple-Drab is a muted, dusty mauve-brown, one of Ridgway's 1912 "drab" names for the flat, low-chroma tans and greys of natural history illustration.

sections.title: A drab with a purple lean
sections.body:
Drab, in Ridgway's system, marks a family of dull, greyish browns rather than any single hue; "purple-drab" adds a faint purple cast to that base [1]. This shade is plate XLV, hue 1'''', tone d, of Ridgway's 1912 standards, read from a scan of an aged plate [1]. We hold no ISCC-NBS or Maerz and Paul record for this exact step, so only Ridgway is cited here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[dark-silver-pink]], [[sweet-pea]], [[silver-pink]] and [[greyish-tan]], at 3.5, 4.5, 4.6 and 4.8 ΔE [1]. The books we hold say nothing about why naturalists needed this particular step, so that origin is undocumented [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, this drab appears in 298, about 1.25 percent, more common than 70 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 54 of 1,674 paintings, at 3.0 times the expected rate for that century, and inside a painting it is most often a light [2].

[[painter:xugu|Xugu]] is its most devoted painter, present in 4 of 16 works here, 6.7 times his museums' baseline [2]. The earliest match is a 1287 painting, over six centuries before Ridgway's 1912 name, so that early hit is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a trace of this named drab, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[fontainebleau]] and [[iris-mauve]] [2].
